pattern.crimePattern: a mother whose son was paralysed by a horse sold as "bombproof" cuts the girth of the dealer's saddle; he cancels his ride and his exercise rider is killed
pattern.notes: Fictional club, trainer and family. Second REAL TARGET case: the cut was meant for the trainer, who cancelled with a migraine at 06:45, after the saddle had been cut. WHERE asks where the crime was done: the tack room.

ob.text: A rider is reported killed in a fall during morning practice at a riding club in Karen: Tajeu Kipaa (29), exercise rider for trainer Gerald Kimani. Suspected riding accident.

facts.text: Tajeu Kipaa, exercise rider, was killed in a fall at morning practice at the Mbagathi Riding Club on Saturday.
Tajeu lay by the goalpost. Gerald's saddle was on the grass, its girth torn free on one side. The horse, Kilele, stopped at once.
Under the flap, two-thirds of the girth's stitching was cut clean (straight thread ends); the last third tore.
Dr. Said: a worn girth tears along its whole length. At a canter the girth went, the saddle slid and Tajeu was thrown head-first into the post. No other horse was near.
Kioko: "Bwana Gerald always rides Kilele in his own saddle on Saturday. Nobody touches that saddle. At quarter to seven Bwana phoned: migraine, let Tajeu ride him in his saddle."
Kioko: he tacked up at seven in front of two grooms and checked the girth for tightness. "I don't lift the flap and look at the stitching. Nobody does."
Phones: Gerald called Kioko at 06:45 for 2 minutes.
Visitors' book: "I. Warsame — 06:10 — to see mare." Then Nicholas Barasa 06:55 and Susan Kimani 06:58. Gerald isn't in it.
Ifrah's groom: Madam looked at the mare for a minute, said she'd left something, and walked to the tack room. She drove off at half past six.
In the tack room (no lock by day): Gerald's peg by the door, saddle soap on the bench, and waxed thread snippets on the floor under the peg.
A vet's report on Shamal from before the sale, addressed to Gerald: "old thoracolumbar injury; bucking under pain likely; not suitable for a novice."
Gerald's sale letter to Zakaria: "Shamal is bombproof, ideal for a young rider." Three months later Shamal threw him at a jump.
Records: Ifrah's car was at the club 06:08–06:31 and home by 06:42; she called Zakaria at 06:33 for 40 seconds.
Zakaria: "Mum called at half past six and said, 'It's done, my son.' I thought she meant she'd filed the new complaint."
In Ifrah's car door pocket: a seam ripper with waxed linen thread and leather dust in its blade.
A yard groom: Nicholas went into the tack room at 06:57 and came out within a minute with a borrowed bridle.
Nicholas's grooms: he was feeding at his own yard across the road from 05:30 until he crossed over at 06:50.
Café receipt: Susan with two owners 07:00–08:00.
The Kimanis' house guard: Gerald was at home all morning with a migraine; his car never left.
The house guard: Susan left the house at 06:50.
Susan: "Gerald gets migraines after a whisky night. He had one on Friday."
Post-mortem: head and neck injuries from a high-speed fall against a post. No heart disease.
Post-mortem: death at 07:50, witnessed.
Lab: the cut stitching matches the seam ripper's blade; the waxed thread in the ripper is the saddle's.
Lab: the leather dust on the blade is the saddle flap's, with the same saddle-soap residue.
Ifrah: "I came to the club at eight for practice. I never went into the tack room."
Ifrah: "Gerald sold my boy a broken horse and swore it was safe. My son will never walk. Tajeu… Tajeu was never supposed to be on that horse."
Ifrah: "I have never held a seam ripper in my life."
Gerald: "I never knew Shamal had any problem. That fall was bad luck."
Gerald: "I had the report. I sold him anyway. It was a lot of money." Then: "It was meant for me. It should have been me."
Nicholas: "I never went near the tack room."
Nicholas: "I borrowed a bridle without asking. I was embarrassed. That's all."
Susan: "I was in the café."

reconstruction.text: Two years ago Gerald sells Ifrah's son Zakaria a grey gelding, Shamal, warranted "bombproof". He has a vet's report on Shamal's old back injury. Three months later Shamal bucks Zakaria off at a jump; he will never walk again.
This month Ifrah finds the old vet's report in a clinic archive. She knows Gerald rides Kilele in his own saddle every Saturday at 07:30.

At 06:10 she signs in "to see mare", looks at the mare for a minute, and walks to the empty tack room. With a seam ripper she cuts two-thirds of the girth stitching on Gerald's saddle, under the flap.

At 06:31 she drives off and calls Zakaria: "It's done." At 06:45 Gerald phones Kioko: migraine, let Tajeu ride. At 07:50, at a canter, the girth tears; the saddle slides and Tajeu is thrown into a goalpost.

clockPlan.note: Two stamps: records on Ifrah's car and phone, and a warrant on her car. Detain her after the search; the tool-mark test (8 h) and the leather trace (12 h) come back inside 24 h.

ui.beatNotes: Cut versus torn. The magnifier on the girth shows thread ends; the player drags a divider along the stitching to mark where the clean cut ends and the tear begins. The notebook converts it to a fact: "Cut two-thirds through by hand. Designed to fail at speed."
